name: Illumination Toolbox
author: James Arrowood (Arrowood Enterprises LLC)
description: Links this player to your Illumination Toolbox account and sends its configuration, with credentials and hardware IDs removed, so the toolbox's xLights AI can help with your show. Optional remote requests need no open port.

privacy.summary: Sends this player's configuration, with passwords removed, to your Illumination Toolbox account and, once you turn remote requests on, lets that account control the player over the internet.

sends.what: setting values without credentials, email addresses or FPP's privacy settings; outputs; warnings
sends.why: so the toolbox and its xLights AI can see how your show is set up

sends.what: the full schedule and config files: co-*/ci-*.json, outputs, overlays, GPIO, presets, proxies
sends.why: so the xLights AI can check your outputs, schedule and wiring against your layout

sends.what: playlists, sequence and music file names, and the list of installed plugins
sends.why: so the toolbox and its xLights AI can see how your show is set up

sends.what: this player's hostname, IP addresses, FPP version and hardware model
sends.why: so the toolbox can tell your players apart and answer for the right FPP version

sends.what: network interface, cape and port status, uptime and sensor readings
sends.why: so the xLights AI can spot a down link, a missing cape or an overheating player

sends.what: free disk space, what is playing now, and the playlists scheduled for the next nine days
sends.why: so the xLights AI can tell whether a show is running, will start tonight, or is out of space

sends.what: the controllers it sends to, whether they answer, and other systems it found on your network
sends.why: so the xLights AI can tell a dark prop from a controller that is off

sends.what: player failover status, when the Player Failover plugin is installed
sends.why: so Control Booth can show which player has the show and let you switch it

sends.what: requests for work and the results of the ones it ran
sends.why: so you can ask for a snapshot, light test, restart or failover switch from the toolbox

systemChanges.what: a systemd timer that checks for configuration changes every five minutes, and a service that asks the toolbox for requests

privacy.other: Nothing is sent until you link the player with a code from your toolbox account. Remote requests are off until you tick the remote requests box on the plugin's page. While it is ticked, the player holds a connection open to api.illuminationtoolbox.com, so no port is opened and nothing on the internet connects to the player, but anyone signed in to the linked toolbox account can, from anywhere, have this player send a fresh snapshot, run a light test on a channel range (even during a show, if they ask with force), stop a test, flag fppd for a restart, or, with the Player Failover plugin installed, take over or hand back the show. Those five requests are all it accepts: no shell commands, files or other FPP pages. A restart request only sets FPP's own restart-required flag, and fppd restarts when you press Restart FPPD or the player next boots. Untick the box to turn requests off again. Anything whose name looks like a password, key or token, and any value shaped like one (a login in a URL, a Bearer token, key=… pairs, email addresses), is replaced on the player before sending. Linking stores a device token in the plugin's data folder, which Unlink and uninstall delete (a Reinstall keeps it). The toolbox keeps the current snapshot plus up to ten earlier ones per player, deleted when you remove the player or delete your account. Privacy policy: https://www.illuminationtoolbox.com/privacy
